items.note: Top-level clause. Subclauses follow. Title not extracted from the licensed copy (structure line only).

items.title: Understanding the Organization and Its Context
items.intent: The organization knows the outside and inside issues that affect what its QMS is for, and it keeps watching them.
items.question: How do you identify the external and internal issues that affect your QMS, and how often do you review them?
evidence: Documented context analysis or issue register with a review date
Records of the last review and the decisions taken
failure_modes: Context analysis absent or generic with no link to the organization
Issues identified once and never reviewed

items.title: Understanding the Needs and Expectations of Interested Parties
items.intent: The organization identifies the interested parties that matter to the QMS and their relevant requirements, and monitors them.
items.question: Who are your relevant interested parties, what do they require from the QMS, and how do you keep that under review?
evidence: List of interested parties and their requirements
Evidence of monitoring, such as customer or regulator correspondence
failure_modes: Requirements of an identified party not reflected in the QMS

items.title: Determining the Scope of the Quality Management System
items.intent: The QMS scope states what products and services it covers, and any requirement judged not applicable is justified.
items.question: What does your QMS scope cover, and how did you justify any requirement you consider not applicable?
evidence: Documented scope with products and services stated
Written justification for each exclusion, linked to the quality manual
failure_modes: Exclusion without justification, or a justification that affects product conformity

items.title: Quality Management System and Its Processes
items.intent: The organization runs its QMS as a set of connected processes.
items.question: Show how your QMS processes are identified and how they interact.
evidence: Process map or list of processes with inputs, outputs and owners

items.title: QMS processes: establishment, operation and improvement
items.intent: Each QMS process has defined inputs, outputs, criteria, resources, responsibilities, risk handling and improvement.
items.question: For one key process, walk me through its inputs, outputs, criteria, resources, responsibilities and how it is improved.
evidence: Process definition for the chosen process
Performance measures and their latest results

items.title: Documented information for the QMS
items.intent: The organization keeps the documented information needed for its QMS to run as planned, including the quality manual content.
items.question: Where is the documented description of your QMS, and how do you know your processes run as planned?
evidence: Quality manual or equivalent covering the listed elements
Records showing processes are carried out as planned
failure_modes: Quality manual missing an element required by the standard
No records to show planned operation

items.note: Top-level clause. Title not extracted from the licensed copy (structure line only).

items.title: Leadership and Commitment
items.intent: Top management takes visible responsibility for the QMS.
items.question: How does top management show accountability and commitment to the QMS?
failure_modes: No evidence of resources or review

items.title: General
items.intent: Top management ensures policy and objectives exist, integration into business processes, the process approach and risk thinking, resources, communication, and support for others to lead.
items.question: Give me examples of what top management has done this year on each element of leadership.
failure_modes: Leadership not visible in any record

items.title: Customer Focus
items.intent: Top management makes sure customer and regulatory requirements are determined and met, and that delivery and conformity performance is measured.
items.question: How does top management know customer and regulatory requirements are met, and what happens when performance falls short?
evidence: Action records when targets are missed
failure_modes: Performance measured but not acted on

items.title: Policy
items.intent: The quality policy exists and is communicated.
items.question: Show me your quality policy and how it is communicated and understood.
evidence: Communication records and staff awareness evidence

items.title: Establishing the Quality Policy
items.intent: The policy suits the organization, sets a framework for objectives, commits to meeting requirements, and commits to continual improvement.
items.question: Walk me through the policy and show where each of its four commitments appears.
evidence: Policy text with the required commitments
failure_modes: Commitment to requirements or to improvement missing

items.title: Communicating the Quality Policy
items.intent: The policy is documented, communicated, understood, and available to relevant parties.
items.question: How do you make the policy available and make sure people apply it?
evidence: Document control record of the policy
Availability to external parties where relevant
failure_modes: Policy not controlled as documented information

items.title: Organizational Roles, Responsibilities, and Authorities
items.intent: Roles and authorities for the QMS are assigned and understood, and a management representative has oversight with access to top management.
items.question: Who is the management representative, what authority do they have, and who holds each QMS responsibility?
evidence: Job descriptions linked to QMS roles

items.note: Top-level clause. Title not extracted from the licensed copy (structure line only).

items.title: Actions to Address Risks and Opportunities
items.intent: Risks and opportunities for the QMS are identified and addressed.
items.question: What are the main risks and opportunities for your QMS, and what did you do about each?
failure_modes: Actions planned but never checked for effectiveness

items.title: Planning for risks and opportunities
items.intent: Planning considers context and requirements to assure the QMS can deliver its results, enhance desirable effects, prevent undesired effects, and improve.
items.question: Show how context and interested party requirements fed into your risk planning.
evidence: Planning record that cites context and interested-party inputs

items.title: Planned actions and their effectiveness
items.intent: Actions are planned, integrated into processes, checked for effectiveness, and proportionate to their impact on conformity.
items.question: Pick one risk action: how was it integrated into a process, and how did you test that it worked?

items.title: Quality Objectives and Planning to Achieve Them
items.intent: Measurable quality objectives exist at relevant levels and are planned and monitored.
items.question: Show me your quality objectives, who owns each, and how progress is tracked.
evidence: Objectives list with measures and targets

items.title: Quality objectives
items.intent: Objectives are consistent with the policy, measurable, relevant to conformity and customer satisfaction, monitored, communicated and updated.
items.question: Choose one objective and show how it meets each of these properties.
evidence: Objective record with measure, target, owner, review date

items.title: Planning how to achieve objectives
items.intent: For each objective the organization records what will be done, the resources, who is responsible, when it will be done, and how results are evaluated.
items.question: For one objective, show the plan: actions, resources, owner, date and evaluation method.
evidence: Objective action plan with all five elements
failure_modes: Plan missing an owner or a date

items.title: Planning of Changes
items.intent: QMS changes are planned and consider their purpose, consequences, the QMS integrity, resources, and responsibilities.
items.question: Describe the last change made to the QMS and how you planned it.
evidence: Change plan or change record covering the four considerations
failure_modes: Integrity of the QMS not considered

items.note: Top-level clause. Title not extracted from the licensed copy (structure line only).

items.title: Resources
items.intent: Resources needed for the QMS are determined and provided.
items.question: How do you decide what resources the QMS needs, and how are gaps handled?

items.title: General
items.intent: Resources are determined for establishing, running, maintaining and improving the QMS, considering internal capability and what must be obtained externally.
items.question: What internal capacity constraints did you identify, and what did you buy in?
evidence: External provider list for resource needs

items.title: People
items.intent: The right people are in place to run the QMS and its processes.
items.question: How do you confirm you have enough people, with the right skills, for each QMS process?

items.title: Infrastructure
items.intent: Buildings, equipment, transport and information systems needed for processes and conformity are provided and maintained.
items.question: Walk me through the infrastructure your key processes depend on, and how it is maintained.
evidence: Maintenance records for equipment and systems
failure_modes: Infrastructure not listed or not maintained

items.title: Environment for the Operation of Processes
items.intent: The work environment, human and physical, is set so processes and conformity are achieved.
items.question: What environmental conditions matter to your processes, and how do you monitor them?
failure_modes: Environment not defined where it affects conformity

items.title: Monitoring and Measuring Resources
items.intent: Monitoring and measuring resources give valid results, traceable where required.
items.question: How do you make sure your measuring resources give valid results?

items.title: General
items.intent: Monitoring and measurement resources are suited to their use, maintained, and their fitness for purpose is documented.
items.question: For one measuring resource, show that it suits its use and remains fit for purpose.
failure_modes: No evidence of fitness for purpose

items.title: Measurement Traceability
items.intent: Where traceability matters, equipment is calibrated or verified against traceable standards, identified, safeguarded, recalled when due, and the register holds the required data. When equipment is found unfit, the validity of past results is reviewed.
items.question: Pick one calibrated instrument: show its calibration, status label, register entry, and what you checked when it was last found out of tolerance.
evidence: Calibration certificate traceable to a national or international standard
Register entry with type, ID, location, method, frequency and acceptance criteria
failure_modes: No assessment of past results after an out-of-tolerance finding

items.title: Organizational Knowledge
items.intent: Knowledge needed for the processes is determined, kept, and made available, and updated as needs change.
items.question: What critical knowledge does your organization depend on, and how is it kept when people leave?

items.title: Competence
items.intent: People whose work affects the QMS are competent, and records prove it.
items.question: How do you determine what competence each role needs, and how do you confirm people have it?
evidence: Evaluation of the effectiveness of training actions

items.title: Awareness
items.intent: People know the policy, objectives, their contribution, the consequences of non-conformity, product safety, and ethics.
items.question: Pick a staff member: what can they tell you about the policy, their contribution and product safety?

items.title: Communication
items.intent: Internal and external communications are planned: what, when, with whom, how, and by whom.
items.question: Show me your communication plan for the QMS and an example of it working.

items.title: Documented Information
items.intent: The QMS has the documented information it requires, and it is controlled.
items.question: How do you decide what documented information the QMS needs, and how is it controlled?

items.title: General
items.intent: The QMS includes required and necessary documented information.
items.question: Show the required documented information for your QMS against the standard's list.
evidence: Cross-reference of required documents to the QMS

items.title: Creating and Updating
items.intent: New or changed documents have identification, a suitable format and media, and review and approval for suitability.
items.question: Show a recent document: its identification, format, review and approval.
evidence: Document with title, date, author or reference, and approval record

items.title: Control of Documented Information
items.intent: Documented information is controlled.
items.question: How do you control documents as a set?

items.title: Availability and protection
items.intent: Documented information is available where and when needed, and protected.
items.question: Show me where a controlled document is available to the person who needs it, and how it is protected.
evidence: Protection controls such as backups and permissions
failure_modes: Document not available at point of use

items.title: Distribution, storage, change, retention and obsolete documents
items.intent: Control covers distribution, storage, version control, retention, prevention of obsolete use, external documents, and electronic data protection.
items.question: How do you stop an obsolete document being used, and how do you control external documents?

items.note: Top-level clause. Title not extracted from the licensed copy (structure line only).

items.title: Operational Planning and Control
items.intent: Operational processes are planned and controlled: requirements, criteria, resources, documented evidence, critical items, and prevention of nonconforming delivery.
items.question: Walk me through how you plan and control one operational process from requirement to delivery.
evidence: Operational plan or quality plan for a sample product

items.title: Operational Risk Management
items.intent: Operational risks are assigned, assessed, communicated, mitigated, and accepted with defined criteria.
items.question: Show me your operational risk process: who owns it, how risks are assessed, and how a risk above your acceptance criteria was handled.
failure_modes: Risks above criteria not mitigated or accepted formally

items.title: Configuration Management
items.intent: Product identity and traceability to requirements are controlled, and documents match the physical product.
items.question: Pick a product: show its identity, traceability to requirements, and that its documents match what is physically present.
failure_modes: Documents differ from the physical product

items.title: Product Safety
items.intent: Product safety is assured through hazard assessment, control of safety-critical items, analysis and reporting of safety events, and training.
items.question: How do you identify safety-critical items and report safety events?

items.title: Prevention of Counterfeit Parts
items.intent: Counterfeit or suspect parts are kept out of delivered product through training, obsolescence monitoring, approved sources, traceability, verification, and quarantine.
items.question: Show how a part is sourced from an approved source and how a suspect part would be quarantined.
evidence: Quarantine and reporting procedure and records

items.title: Requirements for Products and Services
items.intent: The organization understands and agrees its product and service requirements with customers before committing.
items.question: Show how a customer requirement is captured and agreed before you accept an order.

items.title: Customer Communication
items.intent: Customer communication covers product information, enquiries and orders, feedback and complaints, customer property, and contingency requirements.
items.question: Show how a customer complaint came in and was handled.

items.title: Determining the Requirements for Products and Services
items.intent: Product requirements are defined including statutory and regulatory requirements, the organization can meet its claims, and operational risks are identified.
items.question: For one product offered, show its defined requirements and the operational risks you identified.
evidence: Product requirement definition with regulatory requirements
failure_modes: Claims made that the organization cannot meet

items.title: Review of the Requirements for Products and Services
items.intent: A review happens before committing to supply, covering customer, implied, organizational, regulatory and changed requirements.
items.question: Show a recent order review and how it covered regulatory requirements.

items.title: Review before commitment
items.intent: Before commitment, the organization confirms it can meet requirements, negotiates any it cannot meet, and resolves changed order requirements.
items.question: Show a case where a customer requirement could not be fully met, and how it was negotiated.

items.title: Retained review results
items.intent: Review results and new requirements are kept as documented information.
items.question: Where are the results of your order reviews kept?

items.title: Changes to Requirements for Products and Services
items.intent: When product requirements change, documents are amended and affected people are made aware.
items.question: Show a recent requirement change: which documents changed and who was informed.
failure_modes: Documents not amended after a requirement change

items.title: Design and Development of Products and Services
items.intent: A design and development process exists where the organization designs products, or it is recorded that it does not.
items.question: Do you perform any design or development? If not, show the exclusion and how it is justified.
evidence: Design process if design is performed
Exclusion record in the quality manual if it is not
failure_modes: Design exclusion not justified in the quality manual

items.title: General
items.intent: A design and development process exists and is maintained.
items.question: Show your design and development process.

items.title: Design and Development Planning
items.intent: Design stages, reviews, verification and validation, responsibilities, resources, interfaces, customer involvement, and documentation are planned.
items.question: For one design project, show the plan with stages, reviews, verification and validation.

items.title: Design and Development Inputs
items.intent: Design inputs include functional and performance, regulatory, applicable standards, consequences of failure, and obsolescence, are adequate, unambiguous, and conflicts are resolved.
items.question: Show the inputs for a design and how conflicting inputs were resolved.

items.title: Design and Development Controls
items.intent: Design results are defined, reviewed, verified, validated, actions taken on problems, documented, and progression is authorized.
items.question: Walk me through one design review, its verification, its validation, and who authorized progression.

items.title: Design tests
items.intent: Tests are planned, controlled, reviewed, documented, and prove the design meets specification for the operating conditions.
items.question: Show a test plan, the test procedure and the results for one design test.
failure_modes: Tests not planned or acceptance criteria missing

items.title: Design and Development Outputs
items.intent: Design outputs meet inputs, are adequate for later processes, include acceptance criteria, identify essential characteristics and critical items, are approved before release, and define the product data.
items.question: Show the outputs of one design and their approval before release.

items.title: Design and Development Changes
items.intent: Design changes are identified, reviewed, controlled, and customers are notified before implementation where required.
items.question: Show the last design change: its review, authorization, and customer notification.

items.title: Control of Externally Provided Processes, Products, and Services
items.intent: Externally provided processes, products and services conform to requirements, and external providers are controlled.
items.question: Show how you control one external provider, from selection through performance review.

items.title: General
items.intent: The organization controls its external providers: evaluation, selection, performance monitoring and re-evaluation, and risk.
items.question: How do you evaluate, select, monitor and re-evaluate external providers?

items.title: External provider approval and register
items.intent: Approval status decisions, changes, and controlled use are defined; a register holds approval status and scope; performance is reviewed; actions for non-conforming providers are defined.
items.question: Show your provider register with approval status and scope, and the last performance review.
evidence: Provider register with approval status and scope
Action record for a non-conforming provider
failure_modes: Register missing approval status or scope
No action defined for poor providers
